questions.text: A solid right circular cylinder of base radius 7 cm and height 24 cm has a conical cavity of the same base radius and the same height scooped out of one end. Taking π = 22/7, what is the total surface area of the remaining solid?
questions.explanation: The top face is removed by the cavity. Add the cylinder's curved surface (1,056), one base (154) and the cone's curved surface (550): 1,760 cm².
questions.trap: Keeping the top circle even though the cavity occupies all of it.
questions.revise: Hollowed solids: add the cavity surface, remove the opened face
wrongReasons: Left out the circular base at the other end
Added the top circle that was removed by the cavity
Left out the curved surface of the cone

questions.text: A cylindrical vessel with base radius 14 cm holds some water. Three solid iron spheres, each of radius 7 cm, are completely dropped into it and the water does not overflow. By how many centimetres does the water level rise?
questions.explanation: Volume of 3 spheres = 3 × 4/3 π × 7³ = 4π × 343 = 1,372π. Base of the vessel = π × 14² = 196π. Rise = 1,372 ÷ 196 = 7 cm.
questions.trap: Dropping the 4/3 from the sphere's volume.
wrongReasons: Left out the factor 4/3 of the sphere's volume
Used four spheres instead of three
Divided by the vessel's diameter instead of its radius squared

questions.text: The length, breadth and height of a cuboid are in the ratio 5 : 3 : 2 and its volume is 1,920 cm³. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: Edges are 5k, 3k, 2k so 30k³ = 1,920, giving k³ = 64 and k = 4. The edges are 20, 12 and 8 cm. TSA = 2(20×12 + 12×8 + 8×20) = 2(240 + 96 + 160) = 992 cm².
questions.trap: Using the ratio numbers 5, 3, 2 as the edges.
wrongReasons: Gave half of the total surface area
Gave three times the half-surface
Repeated the volume figure

questions.text: A right circular cone of height 18 cm is cut by a plane parallel to its base at a height of 12 cm above the base. What is the ratio of the volume of the smaller cone formed to that of the frustum?
questions.explanation: Cut 12 cm up from the base leaves a small cone of height 6 cm. Volumes of similar cones go as cubes: 1 : 27, so small cone : frustum = 1 : 26.
questions.trap: Giving small : whole, or reading the 12 cm as the small cone's height.
questions.revise: Similar cones: volume ratio = cube of height ratio
wrongReasons: Compared the small cone with the frustum cubing 1 : 2
Gave the ratio of the small cone to the whole cone
Took the small cone as 12 cm tall instead of 6 cm

questions.text: A road roller has a cylindrical drum of diameter 1.4 m and length 2 m. To level a playground it makes 200 complete revolutions. Taking π = 22/7, what is the cost of levelling at ₹3 per m²?
questions.explanation: Curved surface per revolution = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 0.7 × 2 = 8.8 m². For 200 revolutions the area is 1,760 m². Cost = 1,760 × 3 = ₹5,280.
questions.trap: Mixing up diameter and radius.
questions.revise: Rolling cylinder: area covered = curved surface × turns
wrongReasons: Counted only 100 revolutions
Gave the area levelled instead of the cost
Used the diameter 1.4 m in place of the radius

questions.text: The sides of a triangle are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. What is the radius of the circle passing through all three vertices?
questions.explanation: Semi-perimeter s = 21, so the area = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = 84. Circumradius R = abc ÷ 4Δ = (13 × 14 × 15) ÷ (4 × 84) = 2,730 ÷ 336 = 8.125 cm.
questions.trap: Using the inradius formula or assuming a right-angled triangle.
wrongReasons: Gave the inradius instead of the circumradius
Took half of the side 13 cm as the radius
Took half of the largest side as though the triangle were right-angled

questions.text: A toy is a right circular cone of height 24 cm mounted on a hemisphere of the same base radius 7 cm. Taking π = 22/7, what is the total surface area of the toy?
questions.explanation: Slant height = √(7² + 24²) = 25 cm. Curved surface of the cone = πrl = 22/7 × 7 × 25 = 550. Curved surface of the hemisphere = 2πr² = 308. The joined circle is hidden. Total = 550 + 308 = 858 cm².
questions.trap: Adding the base circle that is hidden inside the joint.
questions.revise: Composite solids: count only exposed surfaces
wrongReasons: Counted only the cone's curved surface
Added the hemisphere's flat circle, which is hidden under the cone
Took 3πr² for the hemisphere including its flat face

questions.text: For the distribution shown, what is the median marks?
questions.explanation: N = 80, N/2 = 40. Cumulative frequencies are 8, 20, 35, 60, so the median class is 40–50. Median = 40 + (40 − 35)/25 × 10 = 40 + 2 = 42.
questions.trap: Giving the class mark or the lower limit of the median class.
wrongReasons: Took the mid-value of the median class
Took the lower limit of the median class
Used cumulative frequency before the wrong class

questions.text: For the distribution shown, find the mode using the formula for grouped data.
questions.explanation: The modal class is 30–40 (frequency 18). Mode = L + (f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) × h = 30 + (18 − 9)/(36 − 9 − 12) × 10 = 30 + 9/15 × 10 = 36.
questions.trap: Swapping f₀ and f₂ or giving the class mark.
wrongReasons: Gave the class mark of the modal class
Subtracted the correction instead of adding it
Swapped the preceding and succeeding frequencies

questions.text: The mean of 8 numbers is 12 and the sum of their squares is 1,280. If one of the numbers, 10, is replaced by 18, what is the variance of the new set?
questions.trap: Forgetting that the mean changes with the replacement.
questions.revise: Variance = mean of squares − square of mean

questions.text: The average of 11 numbers is 60. The average of the first six is 58 and of the last six is 63. What is the sixth number?
questions.explanation: The sixth number is counted in both groups. Sum of first six = 348, of last six = 378, total of 11 = 660. The sixth = 348 + 378 − 660 = 66.
questions.trap: Missing that the sixth number is counted twice.
wrongReasons: Took the overall average as the middle number
Took the average of the last six
Took the average of the first six

questions.trap: Treating 20% + 12.5% as one 32.5% discount.

questions.text: A can complete a job in 24 days and B in 36 days. They start working together, but A leaves 6 days before the job is finished, and B completes the rest. In how many days is the whole job finished?
questions.explanation: Let the job take x days. B works all x days and A works x − 6 days. (x − 6)/24 + x/36 = 1. Multiply by 72: 3(x − 6) + 2x = 72, so 5x = 90 and x = 18 days.
steps: B works x days, A works x − 6 days
questions.trap: Giving A and B the same number of working days.
questions.revise: Time and work: unequal working days
wrongReasons: Assumed both worked together for the whole time
Subtracted the 6 days from the joint time of 14.4 and rounded
Added the 6 days to the joint time of 14.4 and rounded

questions.text: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 10 hours and 15 hours respectively, and an outlet C can empty it in 12 hours. All three are opened together. After 4 hours C is closed. How many hours in all does it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: With all open, net rate = 1/10 + 1/15 − 1/12 = 1/12 per hour. In 4 hours, 1/3 is filled. After C is closed the rate is 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6; the remaining 2/3 takes 4 hours. Total = 8 hours.
questions.trap: Forgetting the 4 hours already used.
wrongReasons: Used only the rate with all three pipes open
Ignored the 4 hours of net filling when C was open
Took A's time as the answer

questions.text: A boat takes a total of 9 hours to go 36 km downstream and come back to the starting point. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/h, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.explanation: Let the still-water speed be v. 36/(v + 3) + 36/(v − 3) = 9, so 36 × 2v = 9(v² − 9), i.e. v² − 8v − 9 = 0 and v = 9 km/h. Check: 36/12 + 36/6 = 3 + 6 = 9 hours.
questions.trap: Giving the downstream or upstream speed.
wrongReasons: Gave the downstream speed
Gave the upstream speed
Solved 8v = v² − 9 with the wrong sign

questions.text: A vessel contains 80 litres of pure milk. 16 litres are removed and replaced by water, and this is done twice more (three times in all). How much pure milk is left in the vessel?
questions.explanation: Each operation leaves 64/80 = 4/5 of the milk. After three operations: 80 × (4/5)³ = 80 × 64/125 = 40.96 litres.
questions.trap: Subtracting 16 litres of milk every time.
wrongReasons: Removed 16 litres of milk each time without the shrinking quantity
Applied the factor only twice
Took the removal as 16 litres of milk only once

questions.text: Two circles of radii 13 cm and 15 cm intersect at two points and their common chord is 24 cm long. What is the distance between their centres if the centres lie on opposite sides of the common chord?
questions.explanation: The common chord is perpendicular to the line of centres and is bisected by it. Half-chord = 12. The distances from the centres are √(13² − 12²) = 5 and √(15² − 12²) = 9. On opposite sides, distance = 5 + 9 = 14 cm.
questions.trap: Using 9 − 5 = 4 for the other configuration.
questions.revise: Common chord is bisected perpendicularly by the line of centres
wrongReasons: Gave the distance for centres on the same side
Added the two radii
Subtracted the radii

questions.text: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E on AC such that DE is parallel to BC and AD : DB = 3 : 2. If the area of triangle ADE is 54 cm², what is the area of the trapezium DBCE?
questions.explanation: AD : AB = 3 : 5, so area(ADE) : area(ABC) = 9 : 25. Triangle ABC = 54 × 25/9 = 150 cm². Trapezium = 150 − 54 = 96 cm².
questions.trap: Using the ratio of sides for the ratio of areas.
questions.revise: Similar triangles: areas are in the ratio of the squares of sides
wrongReasons: Used the ratio of sides 3 : 5 instead of the ratio of areas
Gave the area of the whole triangle ABC
Took the trapezium as the 2 : 3 share of the small triangle

questions.text: In the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = (2x + 10)°, ∠C = (4x − 40)° and ∠B = (x + 25)°. What is the measure of ∠D?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°. 2x + 10 + 4x − 40 = 180 gives x = 35. ∠B = 60°, so ∠D = 180 − 60 = 120°.
questions.trap: Giving ∠A, whose value is found on the way.
wrongReasons: Gave ∠C, the angle opposite ∠A
Gave ∠A
Gave ∠B

questions.text: Two circles of radii 9 cm and 4 cm touch each other externally. What is the length of a direct common tangent?
questions.explanation: Distance between centres = 13. Direct common tangent = √(13² − (9 − 4)²) = √(169 − 25) = 12 cm. Equivalent: 2√(Rr) = 2 × 6 = 12.
questions.trap: Choosing the centre distance or the radius difference.
questions.revise: Tangents of two circles: direct vs transverse
wrongReasons: Gave the distance between the centres
Gave the difference of the radii
Took half of the answer

questions.text: If tan θ + cot θ = 3, what is the value of tan³θ + cot³θ?
questions.explanation: tan θ · cot θ = 1. a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b) = 27 − 3 × 3 = 18.

questions.text: From a point on level ground, the tangent of the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 3/4. After moving 70 m closer to the tower, the tangent of the angle becomes 3/2. What is the height of the tower?
questions.explanation: Let the first distance be d and the height h. h = (3/4)d and h = (3/2)(d − 70). So 3d/4 = 3d/2 − 105, giving d = 140 and h = 105 m.
questions.trap: Giving the distance instead of the height.
wrongReasons: Gave the original distance from the tower
Gave the distance moved
Used tan = 4/5 for the first position

questions.text: What is the value of sin²25° + sin²65° + 3 tan5° tan45° tan85° − (sec²60° − tan²60°)?
questions.explanation: sin65° = cos25°, so sin²25° + sin²65° = 1. tan5° tan85° = 1 and tan45° = 1, so the second term is 3. sec²θ − tan²θ = 1. Total = 1 + 3 − 1 = 3.

questions.text: The product of two consecutive positive integers exceeds their sum by 41. What is the smaller integer?
questions.explanation: Let the integers be n and n + 1. n(n + 1) = 2n + 1 + 41, so n² − n − 42 = 0, giving n = 7 (the positive root). Check: 7 × 8 = 56 = 15 + 41.

questions.text: What is the greatest number which divides 245, 413 and 581, leaving the same remainder 5 in each case?
questions.explanation: Subtract the remainder: 240, 408 and 576. HCF(240, 408, 576): 240 = 2⁴ × 3 × 5, 408 = 2³ × 3 × 17, 576 = 2⁶ × 3². HCF = 2³ × 3 = 24, which is greater than the remainder 5.
questions.trap: Dividing the original numbers without subtracting the remainder.
wrongReasons: Took the HCF of the differences instead of the numbers less the remainder
Took only a factor of the HCF
Doubled the HCF
